Limb salvage surgery - Keith Hoskins

By: Nicola De Chaud | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
tonight on Carte Blanche... an alternative to amputation

Summary:
When 20 year old Lewellyn Naiker was diagnosed with cancer he was faced with a choice - lose his leg, or lose his life. He was not willing to undergo an amputation, choosing instead to take his chances with advancing cancer. Dr Keith Hoskins offered him a lifeline through his groundbreaking limb salvage surgery.

Press Release:


Alternatives to amputation
A 20-year-old diagnosed with cancer faces a choice - lose his leg, or lose his life. Not willing to undergo an amputation and with cancer advancing, he clutches at a lifeline offered to him through groundbreaking medical technology. Carte Blanche sees the inner workings of his leg rebuilt with remarkable titanium parts.


Script:


Limb Saving Surgery - Script

Vanessa: I was concerned, if my son’s leg was going to be amputated, how would he react as a youngster cause he’s only 20 and he’s just started life, but on the other hand I wanted his life to be spared

Dr Hoskins: The alternative available mostly in the country at that stage was amputation.

VO: Dr Keith Hosking pioneered limb saving surgery as an alternative.

The big step is that libm savings surgery is possible and it’s possible to save a limb without doing an amputation, we can take a mechano type of set and reconstruct the limb internally to get an leg of appropriate dimensions.... It’s a good feeling, it’s a good feeling

Darren Sweiden: There’s innovation happening aruond the world all the time and if you watch the press and even the local press you’ll see what was the latest innovation showcasing this week”

VO: As a strategist with Discovery Health, Darren is regularly exposed to cutting edge medical innovations.

Darren: And so certainly this was amongst the most exciting that i’d seen some years ago. The outcomes were great the patient reports were good. It’s a very challenging field Dr Hosking works in.

Luwellyn: This operation was something new and different and unique and something not many people have been through

Vanessa:I was so amazed sometimes when you read about different diseases and different conditions that people face, and some of them have to go overeaas to have certain procedures done.

Darren:The fact that locals have got access to international innovations. many of our doctors go overseas and travel to international conferences - having this thought leadership brought home if not sharing what we’ve got locally internationally

VO: Six months earlier Luwellyn Naicker was diagnosed with bone cancer

Luwellyn: It just happened suddenly, one day I was having a shower and I came out and looked at my legs and my left side was slightly bigger than the right

Vanessa: Immediately when the results came through and Dr saw the scan and said to me he has osteosycoma of the femur. I didn’t want to hear it. I tried to blank cancer out. When you hear the C word you don't wanna hear it.

Luwellyn: Yeah, it took me by surprise, I was a bit scared.

Vanessa: I mean he was blunt, he just told us, theres two options, either complete amputation, or limb salvage

Dr Hosking: It’s am emotionally devastating thing for a family and for a young person to be given that diagnosis

When Dr explained to him... he said to me “mommy, if Dr has to amputate my leg, I’m not going to go for surgery I will lie with it until whatever is the outcome

“Why did you choose death over loosing a leg< cause that’s ultimately what you were choosing right” yeah, I was just scared of loosing a leg

Luwellyn underwent three rounds of chemo before deciding on the next step

Vanessa: So they were trying to reduce the tumor, the size of it cause it was 8 cm at that stage. It was very huge”

The chemo delivered the worst possible outcomes

Vanessa: Instead reducing the tumor it grew bigger. Then they started planning surgery

Luwellyn was booked in for surgery in October last year

As a mother it was very difficult for me, it was very difficult decisions to make. I was scared because how would I know if they could save his leg, is it not anywhere else in his body? What’s going to be the outcome. But not knowing, we went into this.

Luwellyn: I just wanted it be over with as soon as possible

Dr Hosking: Certainly this limb sparing with endo-prosthetic replacement it has the lowest complications of all surgeries you would do

up sound : Ok here’s the patients tumor, you can see the swelling and we’ve marked out the line of incisions

Dr Hosking: The procedure is very carefully planned and we’ve done most of the measurements before and we have the benefit of being able to work in association with an engineer, who provides us with a whole modular range of implants, which can be assembled and changed. so we can actually up to a few millimeters alter the relevant limb length. And if necessary we can even proceed to replace an entire bone”

VO: In Luwellyn's case the majority of the proximal femur was removed, with the hip joint affected by the approach.

Up sound: There’s the top half of the femur, about 25 cm... this has now been removed and will now be replaced with a prosthetic device

Vanessa: plus minus 4 to 5 hours we sat in the lounge just sitting and waiting and waiting you know

VO: The defect was replaced with a series of interlinked titanium implants.

Dr Hoskng: in his case he has lost all the muscle in front of his thigh except one but it’s been possible to resect the tumor and still retain a reasonable amount of potential function.

Vanessa: And when Dr walked in and said everything went well, I can’t explain that

Dr Hosking: His rehabilitation will be up to a year and will require regular physiotherapy as well as bio kinetics and we will follow him very closely from an oncological perspective

Vanessa: I don’t know how to explain to you, his recovery was amazing. Within 5 days - on the fifth day after surgery he was actually starting to take a few steps.... So that was really an amazing time for us as a family

Six weeks later Luwellyn was up and walling on two feeling legs

Dr Hosking: From a physical perspective he should be able to walk without a limp. He should be able to play golf, he’ll probably be able to ride a bicycle. YOu need to look at that in terms of the opposite offered operation is, which would have been a through hip amputation, and if you’d done that there would have been no chance of him doing any of those things, plus he would not have been able to have been fitted with a prosthetic limn, so he would be confined to crutches for the rest of his life.

Vanessa: I tell you he was given his second life and I will be ever grateful to Dr Hosking for saving his life, saving his leg, helping him to be able to walk again and I’m sure he’s gonna be a success in whatever he’s gonna do in the future;
